ingestion.description: dlt pipelines (one per source), their modules under sources/, resource docs under docs/, and .dlt/config.toml.

orchestration.description: Scripts that run ingestion and the dbt build, in order.

python_tests.description: pytest tests for ingestion, orchestration and the two maps.

decisions.description: ADRs, including the standing business answers.

contracts.description: ODCS data contracts, one per relation on the contract boundary (the input and boundary layers).

ontology.description: The business ontology and one mapping per Ossie document.

reviews.description: Review findings for triage: intent, proposal, declined or deferred.

proposals.description: Proposed work, read only when an intent's requirement links to it.

key_directories.contracts/: data contracts for the input and boundary relations

notes_for_agents.startup: Read this file first. AGENTS.md says how to work; the skills in .agents/skills/ hold the conventions.
notes_for_agents.new_source: The first source sets the pattern; every later source mirrors an existing entry in `sources` and creates every artifact it lists. Add it to its runner's `orchestrators.<name>.runs` and to that runner's own code. When two sources share a `dataset`, each also declares `produces` (the tables it lands). Add it to `test-map.json` only when it needs its own test module.
notes_for_agents.dlt_environment: Pipelines need VD_DOMAIN_DATA_PLATFORM=duckdb_local, VD_DOMAIN_SECRET_STORE_KIND=local_toml and VD_EPHM_DUCKDB_LOCAL_PATH; orchestration/run_ingest.py sets them.
notes_for_agents.dbt_sources: dbt sources name a schema and never a database: the Studio sandbox is a renamed copy of the Domain file. dbt runs use the dev target.
notes_for_agents.artifact_paths: Every artifact location is declared here: requirement, plan, verification and case_record per intent, design records per model or pipeline (layered: design_record_model) or area. The plugin names an intent's artifacts; this map places them.
notes_for_agents.contracts: Input and boundary layers owe a contract (ADR-0225); internal layers do not. A contract may precede its table with status: proposed. Grain comes from primaryKey, not prose. Boundary tables outside the semantic layer are listed in semantic_exclusions with a reason.
notes_for_agents.reviews_and_proposals: docs/review/ holds review findings for triage; do not read it for build tasks. Read a docs/proposal/ file only when the intent's requirement links to it.
